name: mob-spawn-group-cap
summary: Raise MobHatchery's spawn-group ceiling from 4096, so every map can run on one zone process.

target.note: Identical in Z:/Server and Z:/ServerSource. Every address below was read out of THIS build.

why: MobHatchery holds its spawn groups as an INLINE FIXED ARRAY, not a pointer: ??0MobHatchery
(0x4B3FC0) runs the eh vector constructor iterator over 0x1000 elements of 0x19B8 bytes, then puts
the List<MobBreederGroup> header at a baked +0x19B8000. That is 25.7MB embedded in the object.
The object is static, not heap: 0x5AD987 stores the CONSTANT 0x13389A48 into the global pointer
?mobhatchery@@3PAVMobHatchery@@A, and a CRT init stub does 'mov ecx,0x13389A48; call ctor'. The
PAV in the symbol is a pointer VARIABLE aimed at a static, which is what makes it look heap-allocated.
It cannot grow in place: the array ends at 0x14D41A48 and ?clockwatch@@3VClockWatch@@A begins at
0x14D41A60 -- 24 bytes of headroom.
It CAN be relocated, and that is what this recipe does. All 14 call sites reach the object through
the global pointer; only three instructions carry its raw address. So: append a BSS section with
room, repoint those three immediates at it, and rewrite the two size constants the layout is built
from. No code cave and no allocator call. (It does NOT follow that there is no new runtime failure mode -- see status/measured.)
CEILING: 65534 (see limits). List<MobBreederGroup> is indexed by unsigned short throughout (l_MakeList, l_AllocA,
l_Free all take G). Past that you are retyping the List template, which is a different job.
SIZING: shipped content is 6038 MobRegenGroup records across 88 files (zone 0/1/2/3 = 1628/1962/
1942/261), so one process needs >4096 today, before any 2026 content. 16384 is 2.7x current content
at 103MB -- and one process replaces five, each of which carried its own 25.7MB hatchery inside a
334MB .data image, so consolidating is a large net saving, not a cost.
THE OFFSETS ARE NOT ALL EXACTLY 0x19B8000. Seven sites reach a MEMBER of the List header, so
they bake base+0x4 / +0x8 / +0xC / +0xE (capacity, nodes, freehead, tail). An exact-value
search for 0x19B8000 finds 8 of 15 and the binary then crashes in l_AllocZ with a garbage
handle read from inside the group array. Search the RANGE [base, base+0x400] instead.
0x019B820F in MoveManager::mm_Step is a COINCIDENCE, not a hatchery offset -- do not patch it.

groups.why: List<MobBreederGroup> handles are unsigned short, and 0xFFFF is the INVALID-HANDLE sentinel the overflow guards test (mh_Load 0x4B6595: cmp ax,0xFFFF). l_MakeList (0x4B3B57) also refuses a capacity of 0xFFFF outright -- it nulls the array and returns an unusable list. So 0xFFFE is the last usable capacity, not 0xFFFF. Also: the constructor's node-linking loop is UNROLLED FOUR WAYS (add edx,0x66E0 = 4*0x19B8; four 12-byte node writes per pass) and stores the TRIP COUNT, so groups must be a multiple of 4 or the tail elements are never linked.

new_section.name: .mobhat
new_section.note: Real zero bytes on disk. A virtual-only (BSS) section faulted on first write under Wine on 2026-09-13 -- deterministic, in mh_Load -> l_AllocZ. Costs file size; buys a section the loader must map.

status: WORKING -- boots clean at groups=16384. Verified under Wine 2026-09-13; see measured[].
measured: Docker A/B in fiesta-docker-test (Wine). 'crashes' = EXCEPTION / 'Zone.exe exited' markers.
stock exe            + stock Field.txt (2186 groups)  -> CLEAN     (control, repeated)
stock exe            + all-maps Field.txt (5845)      -> crash before [Message] fieldlist
FINAL patch groups=16384 + stock Field.txt            -> CLEAN, 91 maps loaded
FINAL patch groups=16384 + all-maps Field.txt (5845)  -> clears the group cap; stops later on
'AddInstanceDungeonCluster : Cannot Add[10]'
which is a DIFFERENT, unpatched limit.
Getting there took two misses, both worth keeping:
1. THE UNROLLED TRIP COUNT. The ctor's node-linking loop is unrolled FOUR WAYS (add edx,0x66E0 =
4*0x19B8; four 12-byte node writes per pass; add edi,4; dec [ebp-0x10]) and bakes the ITERATION
count 0x400 = 1024, not the element count. Searching for 0x1000 never sees it. Without this,
only the first 4096 nodes get an element pointer and l_AllocZ hands back an unlinked node.
2. THE OFFSET-INTO-HEADER SITES. Only 8 of 15 sites bake exactly 0x19B8000. Seven more bake
base+0x4/+0x8/+0xC/+0xE to reach List members (capacity, nodes, freehead, tail). An exact-value
search finds 8; the binary then reads a garbage free-list head from inside the group array and
faults in l_AllocZ+0x1F. SEARCH THE RANGE [base, base+0x400], NOT THE VALUE.
Diagnostic that isolated it: patch with groups=4096 (relocation only, count unchanged) -> CLEAN.
groups=4097 -> crash. That proved it was the COUNT, not the relocation, the section, or address space.
Also note: the BSS-vs-materialised question was never actually settled -- the only virtual-only run
used a count that failed for other reasons. materialise=true is simply what has been tested.
